name: feigenbaum-rigorous-enclosures
authority: Research 0129 section 3; this contract authorizes one bounded run and nothing else
question: Which period-doubling thresholds can be rigorously bracketed by interval evaluation of the superstable condition, and where does that direct route stop?
level: External exact rational interval arithmetic with outward rounding; a certified sign change plus the intermediate value theorem gives existence of a root; no floating point in any reported value and no enclosure of the Feigenbaum constants is claimed
domain: The logistic map f_r(x) = r x (1 - x) on r in [0,4], the superstable condition h_k(r) = f_r^(2^k)(1/2) - 1/2 = 0, exact rational interval arithmetic rounded outward to a declared decimal grid, and the period-doubling thresholds r_k for k from 1 to a declared maximum level
quantifiers: Every level in the declared list, with the endpoint signs evaluated in interval arithmetic
Every bisection step until the midpoint sign stops being definite
Every reported bracket endpoint compared exactly against the closed form 1 + sqrt5 at level one
acceptance: The interval arithmetic is self-tested: a product of intervals encloses the exact product, and outward rounding widens rather than narrows
A level is certified only when the interval evaluations at the two bracket endpoints have strictly opposite signs, so the existence of a root follows from the intermediate value theorem
Every certified bracket at level one contains the exact closed form 1 + sqrt(5), checked by exact integer comparison rather than by decimals
The level at which certification stops is reported with its reason, and a coarser grid is run as a control so that the number of certified levels is seen to depend on the declared precision
The interval width amplification per iteration is measured and reported, and the run never lets a width grow past the declared cap
Enclosures of the ratios delta_k for the levels whose thresholds are certified are reported, and no enclosure of delta or alpha themselves is claimed
protected: The three earlier Feigenbaum rounds are frozen and are not rewritten; this round reads one of them as its starting bracket and says so
Existence of a root in a certified bracket does not identify it as the cascade threshold of that level, and uniqueness is not claimed
No enclosure of the Feigenbaum constants is claimed, and the reason the direct route cannot supply one is stated
No metric, Arakelov, Monge-Ampere, mirror or Calabi-Yau content is introduced
No native Rust witness, library admission or Seal follows from this calibration
residual: This certifies brackets for the low levels only and measures why the direct route stops. It is not a rigorous enclosure of the Feigenbaum constants: the thresholds are rigorously bracketed, but the limit of their ratios is not, and no bound on the distance to that limit is available here. Turning this into a proved enclosure of the constants needs the period-doubling operator in a function space with a Newton-Kantorovich bound, which is the next step and is not attempted here.
